sections.h2: Which Huntington office bills my property tax?
sections.html:
The work divides in two. The Assessor values the more than 72,500 parcels in the town and its incorporated villages, and the Receiver of Taxes sends the bills and takes the money. The Town Board appoints the Assessor, while the Receiver is elected.

The Receiver's office is in Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street, Huntington, NY 11743. It collects for the town, Suffolk County, the school districts and other taxing districts, and it also takes Dix Hills Water District payments. The office does not set the rate or the assessment. It carries out collection under the New York Real Property Tax Law and the Suffolk County Tax Act. The office number is 631-351-3217.

Counter hours for payments are 9 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday. The general office stays open from 8 am to 5:30 pm.

sections.h2: When Huntington property taxes are due
sections.html:
Huntington sends one bill a year, in the second week of December. For 2026/27, the first half is due January 10, 2027 and the second half May 31, 2027. A due date on a weekend slides forward, and January 10, 2027 itself falls on a Sunday. Town Hall also lists extended payment hours until 7 pm on June 1, 2027.

Two groups get extra days on the second half. Owners receiving Basic STAR have until June 4, 2027. So do seniors on the Senior Low-Income exemption or Enhanced STAR, though after June 1 they can only pay by mail or at the counter.

A federal postmark change effective December 24, 2025 means a mailbox drop may not receive a same-day postmark. Only a hand stamp at a post office counter is guaranteed, and the tax office cannot waive penalties for a payment that is neither postmarked nor received on time. Safer routes are paying online, calling the payment line at (877) 690-3729 with jurisdiction code 2012 and your 8 digit bill number, paying at Town Hall, or using the locked black box at Town Hall. Online payments carry third-party fees.

sections.h2: What a late first-half payment costs
sections.html:
Interest on the first half starts at 1% on January 11 and climbs one point each month until it reaches 5% in the last three weeks of May.

Interest on a late first-half payment, 2026/27
Paid betweenInterest
December 1 to January 10None
January 11 to February 101%
February 11 to March 102%
March 11 to April 103%
April 11 to May 104%
May 11 to May 315%

After May 31 the town can no longer take the money. Payment, with a 5% penalty and monthly interest of 1% counted from February 1, goes to the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, phone (631) 852-3000.

File a written complaint with the Town Assessor's Office by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May. In 2027 that falls on May 18. The Assessor's Office is in Room 100 of Town Hall, and the number is (631) 351-3226.

  • March 1 is the taxable status date, and property is valued as of its condition that day.
  • May 1 is when the tentative roll is set and opened for public inspection.
  • Complaint forms and a fact sheet are available after April 1, and the town accepts only an originally signed copy. Faxed or emailed forms are rejected.
  • If the Board of Assessment Review denies the complaint, a court challenge follows. New York State lists a $30 fee for Small Claims Assessment Review, with a filing window of 30 days from the final roll.

Suffolk County boards meet on the third Tuesday in May, which is earlier than the fourth Tuesday used in most of the state. A seller who waits for the later date will miss the Huntington window.

The Assessor's Office handles every exemption, and applications are due by March 1 to count on the following December's bill. The main programs are:

  • Senior Citizens Limited-Income, for owners aged 65 or older. The income ceiling is $58,400 for both town and county, with documented medical costs deductible.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income, with the same March 1 filing date.
  • Military service exemptions: Alternative, Cold War, Eligible Funds and Gold Star Parent.
  • Home Improvement, which phases in the added assessment from a renovation over nine years, up to 400 in assessment.

Basic and Enhanced STAR are state programs. For questions, call the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance at 518-457-2036. Exemptions are tied to the owner, so a buyer has to apply on their own after closing.

sections.h2: If Huntington tax is owed, how does a sale work?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property, so the closing needs a current figure. The Receiver's office keeps the tax rolls, including changes of ownership and a list of taxes in arrears. Ask the office, before a contract is signed, which half of the current bill is paid.

If the 2026/27 bill is still open when you list, plan around two dates. Before May 31, 2027 the Receiver takes the payment. After that date the tax, penalty and interest must go to the county comptroller in Riverhead, and the amount keeps growing by 1% a month. Have the payoff written onto the closing statement, using the figure the Receiver or the comptroller gives you in writing.

Dix Hills Water District payments also go through the Receiver's office, so a Dix Hills seller should ask whether a water district balance sits beside the tax bill. A buyer paying cash can close on a short timeline and settle the tax at the table. That is useful for owners in Huntington Station, Dix Hills or Greenlawn whose bills have fallen behind and who want the matter closed without waiting on a listing.

Huntington sits on the North Shore of Long Island, with Long Island Sound to the north and Nassau County to the west. Its four incorporated villages are Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport, and hamlets include Dix Hills, Melville, Commack, Greenlawn and Huntington Station.

The town counts 205,891 residents in July 2025 and 71,542 households. Owners live in about 88.7% of homes, which are valued at $715,600 at the median. Household income reaches $168,029, and median rent is $2,358.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Huntington property tax due in 2027?
faqs.a: May 31, 2027, with extended hours on June 1, 2027. Owners on Basic STAR, the Senior Low-Income exemption or Enhanced STAR have until June 4, 2027.

faqs.q: Where do I pay late Huntington property tax after May 31?
faqs.a: Send it to the Suffolk County Comptroller at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901. The comptroller's number is (631) 852-3000, and the amount includes a 5% penalty plus monthly interest.

faqs.q: What is Grievance Day in Huntington?
faqs.a: Grievance Day lands on the third Tuesday of May, so May 18 in 2027. The Assessor's Office must receive an originally signed complaint on or before that day, and fax or email copies are rejected.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a senior exemption in Huntington?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at (631) 351-3226 to join the mailing list, and file the application with proof of income by March 1. The income limit is $58,400.

faqs.q: Does the Huntington Receiver of Taxes set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The office collects and distributes tax. It does not determine the rate or the assessment.
